Check a supplement site before a release

Source: R/check-supplement.R
check_supplement.Rd

check_supplement() looks for problems that can break a release of a site, publish files that must stay private, or publish the template's placeholder values in place of the author's. It changes no file. It prints each problem it finds and returns all of them as a data frame.

Usage

check_supplement(path = ".", web_links = FALSE, renv_lock = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The folder of the site.

web_links

TRUE to also request each web address on the pages in docs/ and give the "web-link" rows. This needs a network. The default, FALSE, makes no web request.

renv_lock

TRUE to also compare the R and package versions in the stored output of each report with the site's renv.lock and give the "renv-mismatch" rows, and to give the "renv-missing" rows for attached packages that renv.lock does not name. With an renv profile, the check reads the profile's lockfile instead, as the "renv-mismatch" item says. The default, FALSE, does not read renv.lock.

Value

A data frame with one row per problem and the character columns check, file (the path in the site), and problem, invisibly. It has zero rows when the function finds no problem. Its skipped attribute names the git checks ("large-file", "saved-object", and "ignored-output") that did not run, and is empty when they ran.

Details

The checks, by the value in the check column:

  • "large-file": a file larger than 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes), which GitHub refuses. A symbolic link, or on Windows a junction, is not counted, because git stores only the link.

  • "saved-object": a saved R object (.rds, .rda, .rdata, .qs, or .qs2, in any letter case). A fitted model saved this way can hold the data it was fitted to.

  • "ignored-output": a file that git ignores in figures/, docs/, or _freeze/, so that a release leaves it out of the published site. The check takes each regular file in these folders, and in the folders in them, that is reached without passing through a symbolic link or, on Windows, a junction, and whose path holds no name that starts with .. The file gets a row when git neither tracks it nor lists it as untracked, because its ignore rules exclude it, such as a rule in .gitignore or .git/info/exclude. A file that git tracks gives no row, also when a rule matches it. The copy of a data file in docs/data/ gets a row when a rule also matches the copy, as the template's rule for .rds files does. The problem text says to change the rule for a file that the site must publish, and to remove the source of a private file and render again.

  • "no-stored-output": a .qmd report directly in analyses/, not in a folder inside it, with code and no stored output in _freeze/. A full render then runs its code, which needs the data. A report has code when a line starts a code chunk: any mix of spaces, tabs, and > characters, three or more backticks, optional spaces or tabs, then { and a name. The name is the longest run of an ASCII letter followed by ASCII letters, digits, _, or .. Any text without } can follow the name, then }, and the line ends with optional spaces or tabs. A chunk named ojs, mermaid, or dot, in any letter case, does not count, because Quarto starts no engine for it. Every other name counts, such as {bash} or {sql}, and so does a chunk in a report whose front matter sets engine: markdown. Quarto also reads other white space, line breaks included, between the backticks and { and after }. It lets the text after the name run across lines, and it starts a line after U+2028 or U+2029. Such chunk starts are not found. A nul byte in a report counts as a character that is none of those this rule names. A report with no chunk that counts also has code when it has inline R code on one line and the top-level engine in its own front matter is knitr. Inline R code is a backtick, then r and a space or #, or {r} and a space, then text with no backtick, then a backtick. Inline code that spans lines is not found, nor is inline code with a tab after {r}, which knitr also runs. Nor is knitr that a knitr key, execute: engine, an included file, or _metadata.yml turns on. A report has no stored output when _freeze/analyses/<name>/execute-results/ holds no file other than hidden files and the files in hidden folders.

  • "stale-output": a .qmd report directly in analyses/, from the same list of reports, whose stored output was made from other text than the report holds now. The check reads as JSON each file whose name ends in .json and does not start with ., directly in _freeze/analyses/<name>/execute-results/. Quarto writes the MD5 of the report's text there as the top-level hash. The report gets one row when such a hash is one text value that differs from the MD5 of the report's bytes with each CR LF pair read as LF. It also gets one row, which says that the source hash of its stored output cannot be read, when such a file does not parse, its top level is not an object, or its top-level hash is missing or is not one text value. When one file cannot be read and another differs, the one row has this text. A report that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, gives no row. Quarto 1.10.19 hashes only the report file, so a change in a file that the report includes, in _quarto.yml or _metadata.yml, or in the data gives no row. Reports in folders inside analyses/ are not read. Quarto reads a report as UTF-8 and hashes each byte that is not valid UTF-8 as U+FFFD, so such a report gets a row after each render. The row names, by their paths from the site folder in byte order, each of these files whose hash differs, or in the "cannot be read" text only each file whose hash cannot be read. Each path stands between double quotes, with a \ before each \ and " in it, so that a name that holds a comma and a space reads as one file. The "cannot be read" text ends with the render steps and then a delete step. It says that if the row stays after the render steps, the files can be from a format that the report no longer renders, or damaged. Then it says to delete them, render the whole site, and commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. Quarto keeps the file of a format that the report no longer renders, such as docx.json, with its old hash. So when every hash can be read and another of these files has a hash equal to that MD5 of the report, the row also says that the files that differ can be from a format that the report no longer renders. If so, delete them, render the whole site, and commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. If not, follow the render steps that the row gives after the hint.

  • "stale-script": a .qmd report directly in analyses/, from the same list of reports, whose stored output was made with other text of _scripts/report.R than the site holds now. print_environment() in the template's _scripts/report.R ends the Computing environment section with the line Shared report code: _scripts/report.R, MD5 and the file's MD5, with each CR LF pair read as LF. The check reads the same .json files as the "stale-output" check. In the top-level result.markdown text of each, it finds that text and the 32 characters after it, when they are lowercase hex. The report gets one row when one of these hashes differs from the MD5 of the site's _scripts/report.R, read the same way. The row names the files that hold a hash that differs, in the same way as the "stale-output" row, and gives the render steps. When another of these files holds at least one such hash and all of its hashes match, it also says that the files that differ can be from a format that the report no longer renders, with the same delete steps as the "stale-output" row. A report whose stored output holds no such hash gets no row, for example a report without the Computing environment section, or one rendered before the site had a _scripts/report.R that prints the line. A file that does not parse or has no result.markdown text holds no hash. Such a line anywhere in result.markdown counts, also one that the report prints from other text, such as the stored output of another report. A report that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, gives no row. When the site has no _scripts/report.R that can be read, for example when the file is missing, is a folder, is a link to a missing file, or cannot be opened, the check gives no row. The hash covers only _scripts/report.R, not files that it reads.

  • "renv-mismatch": only with renv_lock = TRUE, a .qmd report directly in analyses/, from the same list of reports, whose stored output names an R or package version other than the one that the site's renv.lock records. The check reads the same result.markdown text as the "stale-script" check. In it, it reads the versions in the forms that print_environment() prints. From sessioninfo::session_info(), these are the package table after a line that starts with ─ Packages or - Packages, read at the positions of the package and version columns of its header line, and the setting line that starts with version, spaces, and R's version string, such as R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) or R version 4.6.1 Patched (...). From utils::sessionInfo(), these are the first line that starts with R's version string, and the name_version entries on the lines that start with [1], [2], and so on, after any spaces, after other attached packages: and after loaded via a namespace (and not attached):. A line that holds an ANSI escape is not read, and output that knitr prints after a comment prefix such as ## is not found. A CR at the end of a line is ignored.

    A package differs when one of its stored versions is not equal to the Version that renv.lock records for it under Packages. The R version differs when a stored R version is not equal to the Version under R. Versions are compared as package_version() values, so 1.0-5 equals 1.0.5. A package that renv.lock does not record, such as a base package, is not compared; the "renv-missing" check gives a row for such a package that a report attached. Nor is a version that package_version() cannot read on either side, such as devel, or the R version when renv.lock records none. A development build of R prints R Under development (unstable), which the check does not read as an R version. The report gets one row. It names the files that hold a version that differs, in the same way as the "stale-script" row. Then it names the R versions that differ, and each package that differs, in byte order of name, each with its stored versions that differ, in version order and each version once, and the version in renv.lock. It says to run renv::restore() and take the render steps, or, if the library now holds the versions of the report, to run renv::snapshot() and commit renv.lock. When another of these files holds a version that is compared and none that differ, the row also gives the format hint and delete steps of the "stale-script" row. A file that does not parse holds no versions, and a report that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, gives no row.

    renv.lock gets one row of its own, and no report gets a row, when it is a folder, a link to a missing file, a file that cannot be opened, text that is not valid UTF-8, text that is not JSON, or JSON whose top level or Packages is not an object. So does a file that repeats a key that the check reads, such as two records of one package, because jsonlite keeps both and renv may read the other. A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is skipped. A package record is named by its Package text, or by its key when it has none, and a record with no Version text is left out of the comparison. A site with no renv.lock gets no row, and the function says that it skipped this check and the "renv-missing" check. release_supplement() does not run this check, so its rows never stop a release.

    renv.lock also gets a row of its own when the check reads it but a folder or file in its path is listed under another spelling, such as Renv.lock. renv finds such a file only where the file system treats both spellings as one name, as macOS and Windows do for letter case by default, and write_dockerfile() refuses it. The row names the path as listed, when it can tell, and says to rename it. The reports still get their rows.

    In this item and the next, renv.lock is the lockfile that renv 1.3.1 picks for the site's renv profile. The profile's name comes from the RENV_PROFILE environment variable of the R session that runs the check, when it is not empty. Otherwise it comes from the first line of renv/profile in the site folder, untrimmed, when that file exists. The name default, an empty name, or no name means no profile, and the lockfile is renv.lock in the site folder. With a profile, the lockfile is renv/profiles/<name>/renv.lock, with the name joined as given. The function then says which profile it picked and where the name came from. When RENV_PROFILE and the first line of renv/profile give the same name, as in an R session that the site's renv/activate.R started, because it copies that line into RENV_PROFILE, the message names both. The rows name that path where they name renv.lock, and they say to run the renv commands with the profile active. When renv/profile is read and is a folder or a file that cannot be opened, it gets one row of its own, and no report gets a row. The check does not read RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE or RENV_PATHS_RENV, which renv reads to move the lockfile and the renv folder.

  • "renv-missing": only with renv_lock = TRUE, a report from the same list whose stored output shows that it attached a package that the site's renv.lock does not name under Packages, so renv::restore() does not install it from renv.lock. The check reads the same .json files, in the same forms, as the "renv-mismatch" check. A package counts as attached when a line of the sessioninfo package table has * under the * of the table's header line, or when it is an entry after other attached packages: in utils::sessionInfo() output. A package that is loaded and not attached, such as knitr during a render or a package after loaded via a namespace (and not attached):, gives no row, since the render tools and not the report's code can load it. renv's default (implicit) snapshot records the packages that renv::dependencies() finds in the project, with their dependencies. A package that the user's R profile attaches during a render, or that renv's settings leave out of renv.lock, also gives a row, which renv::snapshot() and a new render do not clear. renv.lock names a package when it holds a record under Packages with that name, whatever its Version. A record is named as for the "renv-mismatch" check, and a record whose name is empty names no package. The report gets one row. It names the files that show such a package attached, in the same way as the "renv-mismatch" row, and each such package once, in byte order of name. It says to run renv::snapshot() and commit renv.lock, or, if the report no longer uses the packages, to take the render steps. When another of these files holds a package table or list and attaches none of them, the row also says that these files can be from a format that the report no longer renders, with the delete steps of the "renv-mismatch" row. A report that cannot be read gives no row. When renv.lock is missing, this check gives no row, and the function says that it skipped it. When renv.lock cannot be read, this check gives no row, and the one "renv-mismatch" row for renv.lock reports the problem. The "renv-missing" rows come after the "renv-mismatch" rows. release_supplement() does not run this check.

  • "leftover-output": a folder directly in _freeze/analyses/, whose name does not start with ., that no file or folder in analyses/ names. A name in analyses/ names the folder when, cut before its last . (the whole name when it holds no .), it equals the folder's name with letter case ignored: the case of ASCII letters always, and the case of other letters as tolower() reads it in the session's locale. In a name that is not valid UTF-8, only the case of ASCII letters is ignored. A name stored in another Unicode form, composed or decomposed, does not match. Quarto 1.10.19 keeps a report's folder after the report is deleted or renamed. The row says to delete the folder, render the whole site, and commit _freeze/ and docs/, and for a deleted or renamed report also its old path and _quarto.yml. Folders inside subfolders of _freeze/analyses/ and folders directly in _freeze/ are not read. A file or folder in analyses/ of the same name, such as <name>.R, hides a leftover folder. So does a report whose name differs only in letter case, as after a report is renamed only in letter case on Linux.

  • "missing-script": the site has no file _scripts/report.R, and a .qmd report directly in analyses/, from the same list of reports, names it. The template's example report and each report from add_report() read it. The file counts as missing when file.exists() is FALSE for it, when it is a folder, or when it is a link whose chain of links ends on a missing file, a folder, or a loop, or one that fs::path_real() cannot resolve. So a file link to a missing file counts as missing on Windows too, where file.exists() is TRUE for it. A link whose path is not valid UTF-8 counts as there. A report names the file when one of its lines holds _scripts, with no ASCII letter, digit, _, or . right before it, then a separator, then report.R, with no ASCII letter, digit, _, or . right after it. Each such _scripts on the line can start the match, so _scripts_old/x and _scripts/report.R names the file. The separator is /, \, or \\, or it is a " or ', a , with any spaces or tabs on each side, and a " or ', after an optional /, \, or \\. So source(file.path(site, "_scripts", "report.R"), local = TRUE) and _scripts/report.R name the file, and _scripts_old/report.R, _scripts/old-report.R, and file.path("_scripts", "x", "report.R") do not. A . right after report.R, as at the end of a sentence, stops the match. A line of prose or a comment also counts. One row names each such report by its path from the site folder, in byte order, between double quotes with a \ before each \ and " in it, and says to copy the template's file from system.file("template", "_scripts", "report.R", package = "supplement") and commit it. A site made before the template had the file gives no row when its reports do not name it. A line in a file that the report includes is not read, a line of another form, such as source("report.R") or a call that puts _scripts and report.R on two lines, does not count, and the letter case of both names must match. Reports in folders inside analyses/ are not read, and a report that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, names nothing. On a disk that ignores letter case a file such as _scripts/Report.R reads as _scripts/report.R, so it gives no row there.

  • "not-rendered": the site has no docs/ folder.

  • "broken-link": an href, src, or xlink:href link on a page in docs/ to a file that is not in docs/, or to a folder there with no index.html, or a link that ends with / to a file. A page that cannot be read, such as a link to a missing file, also counts. Pages in every folder of docs/ are read, hidden files and folders (names that start with .) included. A symbolic link to a folder, or on Windows a junction, is not entered. A page in a folder that such a link points to is read once, at its own path, when the folder is in docs/. A symbolic link in docs/ to a page file in docs/ is read as a page of its own. A symbolic link or junction in docs/ whose target exists and resolves to a place outside docs/ gives a row of its own, because the published site does not have its target. So a link to such a link also gives a row. A page that it points to, or a page in a folder that it points to, is not read. A link on a page whose path passes through or ends at such a link also counts. For a link to a folder, the folder's index.html is part of that path. A symbolic link or junction that resolves to docs/ or a place in it gives no row of its own. Links that start with /, #, or a scheme such as https: are not checked here, except a # link under a local base (below). Only the "web-link" check, with web_links = TRUE, requests web addresses. GitHub Pages matches letter case, so a link whose case differs from the file name counts as broken, also on a disk that ignores case. A link that also differs from the name in Unicode form (for example é written as e plus an accent) is not caught.

    Links are read from start tags only, as a browser reads them. Comments, <!...> and <?...> markup, end tags, and the text of <script>, <style>, <textarea>, and <title> elements are skipped, and so is page text such as <code> text. These parts end as the HTML Standard says, except as listed below. A comment ends at the > of <!--> or <!--->, and otherwise at its first --> or --!>. </ followed by a character that is not an ASCII letter or > starts a bogus comment, which ends at the next >. An end tag is read through its attributes, so a > in a quoted value does not end it. In the text of a script, <!-- starts escaped text, which ends at the next -->, whose dashes can be those of the <!--. In escaped text, <script followed by a space, tab, line break, form feed, /, or > makes the next </script> part of the text, unless a --> comes first. Any other </script> ends the script. Attribute names match in any letter case, and only whole names count, so data-href and data-src are not read. A value can be in double quotes, in single quotes, or unquoted, where it runs to the next space or >. An attribute with no =, such as <a href>, has an empty value and is not checked. A start tag that the end of the page cuts off is not read, as a browser drops it. A page whose markup goes past the limits of the PCRE pattern engine gives one row that says so, in place of its link rows. Such a page holds millions of - in one comment, millions of < in the text of one script, style, textarea, or title element (about 5 million did, in a page of 20 MB), or millions of attributes in one tag. Script text with millions of </ or <!, or, after <!--, millions of <s or of separate runs of -, can reach the limits sooner. Each value is handled in this order: character references are decoded; spaces, tabs, line breaks, and form feeds at its ends are removed and tabs and line breaks inside it are dropped; links with a scheme, /, or # at the start are skipped, except a # link under a local base (below); then % escapes are decoded. The decoded references are &amp;, &lt;, &gt;, &quot;, and &apos; (in lower case, with the ;), and number references such as &#38; or &#x26; with the ; that name a code point from 1 to 0x10FFFF, other than a surrogate or 128 to 159. A row shows the link after the references are decoded, the ends removed, and the tabs and line breaks inside it dropped.

    A <base> tag changes where the links of its page lead. Only the first <base> tag with an href counts, and its href is not a link itself. Its value is read as a link value is. If the value is empty, starts with # or ?, or starts with data: or javascript: in any letter case, links resolve against the page's own folder, as with no base. If the value has another scheme, such as https:, or starts with /, the page's relative links are not checked. Any other value is a local base. Relative links then resolve against the folder of the base address, with its ? and # parts removed. A base whose last part is . or .. names a folder. A link of only a # or ? part resolves to the base address itself. A row shows the link before it is resolved against the base.

    These are the main cases where the check reads a page differently from a browser. Every other reference (such as &eacute;, &AMP;, or &#38 with no ;) stays as written. Other control characters at the ends of a link, such as &#1;, stay, while a browser removes them. The text of <noscript>, <xmp>, <iframe>, <noembed>, <noframes>, and <plaintext> elements is read as markup, and so is the text of a <![CDATA[...]]> section after its first >. The four skipped elements are also skipped inside <svg> and <math>. The end tags of those four elements end at their first >, also inside a quoted value. A <base> tag inside <template>, or inside <svg> but not in its <foreignObject> or <desc>, counts as a base, though a browser does not use it. A base with a scheme whose address a browser cannot read, such as http://, leaves the page's relative links unchecked, while a browser resolves them against the page's own folder. A \ in a base is not read as /, while a browser reads it so. An empty link, such as href="", is not checked, also under a local base, while a browser resolves it to the base address. Under a base with another scheme or a leading /, a browser can follow the page's relative links to a place that the check does not read, and the check does not check them. A " or ' with no closing quote starts an unquoted value, so the next > ends that tag and it is read, where a browser reads on to the end of the page and drops the tag. A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is read as text such as <e9>; outside a quoted value, its > ends the tag, so an unquoted value keeps the <e9 part and the later attributes of that tag are not read. A second attribute of the same name is also read.

  • "web-link": only with web_links = TRUE, a web address on a page in docs/ that fails. The check reads the same pages and values as the "broken-link" check, in the same way, and keeps each value that starts with http: or https: in any letter case, with any # part removed. So the cases above where that check reads a page differently from a browser apply here too: a reference such as &eacute; stays as written, and the address is requested with it. A link that starts with // has no scheme and is not requested. A space in an address is sent as %20, as a browser sends it. A page that the "broken-link" check cannot read gives no "web-link" row. Each address is requested once (addresses that differ only in letter case count as two), one after another, with a HEAD request that follows redirects and waits up to 10 seconds. A site with many addresses can take minutes. An address gets a row when the request fails, such as for an unknown host, a timeout, or a certificate error, or when the last response has a status of 400 or above. The row names the first page, in byte order of path, that links the address. For status 401, 403, 405, or 429, the row says that the server refused the check's request and that the link can still work in a browser, since some servers answer a script or a HEAD request that way. release_supplement() does not run this check, so its rows never stop a release.

  • "unpublished-figure": a paper figure that the last render did not copy into docs/. The check takes each regular file in figures/, and in the folders in it, that is reached without passing through a symbolic link or junction, and whose path holds no name that starts with .. The file gets a row when the same path under docs/figures/ is not a regular file, or when the MD5 of its bytes differs. A render copies into docs/figures/ the files that figures/ holds when the render starts, so a figure saved under a new name or changed after the last render gets a row, and a full render or a render of a report by name clears it. Hidden files are not compared, though Quarto copies them too.

  • "doi-mismatch": the DOI in CITATION.cff differs from the one that write_citation() writes from _supplement.yml, or the DOI badge on docs/index.html differs from zenodo.version-doi (or zenodo.concept-doi when that is empty). A home page whose source uses {{< supplement-doi >}} but that shows no badge, while _supplement.yml has a DOI, also counts. So does a CITATION.cff that cannot be read or is not a YAML map (a link to a missing file included), and a DOI in CITATION.cff or on the badge that is not a DOI.

  • "placeholder": a template value that the author has not replaced, so that a release would archive it. The check compares the site with the template that the installed package holds:

    • _supplement.yml gets one row when paper-title, citation, or contact equals the template's value, or an authors entry has the family and given of a template author. Values are compared with each run of white space read as one space and the ends removed. A value that is not one text value does not count. The row names the fields.

    • _quarto.yml gets a row for the line href: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO, index.qmd for the line ## Before your first commit, LICENSE.md and LICENSE-CC-BY.md for the line Copyright (c) YEAR AUTHORS, and README.md, SUPPLEMENT.md, and _README.md for the line Website: https://OWNER.github.io/REPO/. SUPPLEMENT.md is for a site made before the template's guide moved to GUIDE.md: when that site's first render found a README.md, it wrote the guide to SUPPLEMENT.md. Spaces, tabs, and a carriage return at the ends of a line are ignored. A file that is missing, a folder, not UTF-8 text, or that cannot be read gives no row.

    • analyses/example.qmd and data/example.csv each get a row when their text equals the template's copy. analyses/example.qmd also gets one when its text equals the example report of an earlier version of the template. The text counts as equal when it differs only by a UTF-8 byte order mark at its start, CR LF or CR line ends in place of LF, or no line break at its end, as an editor can save an unchanged file. A file that cannot be read gives no row.

    Only a whole value or a whole line counts, so a value that keeps part of a placeholder, such as a citation with (Year) in it, gives no row. A site made from an older version of the template, whose placeholders differ from the installed ones, gives no row for them. The example report is the exception.

The "large-file" and "saved-object" checks look at the files that git tracks or does not ignore, which git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard lists, so files that .gitignore blocks are left out. The "ignored-output" check reads the files that git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard lists in figures/, docs/, and _freeze/. For these three git checks the function runs git only to read: git --version, git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree, and git ls-files. When git is not on the PATH, one of these commands fails, or the folder is not in a git work tree, it skips these three checks and says so.

Errors

The function stops with an error of class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-empty string, or web_links or renv_lock is not TRUE or FALSE.

  • supplement_error_no_metadata: path holds no _supplement.yml.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _supplement.yml, as for write_citation().

  • supplement_error_no_map: _supplement.yml has no supplement: map.

  • supplement_error_field_type: a DOI in _supplement.yml is not one text value, or zenodo is not a map.

  • supplement_error_doi: a DOI in _supplement.yml is not a DOI.

See also

write_citation() to write CITATION.cff again.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "check-example")
create_supplement(site)
#> ✔ Made a supplement site in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/check-example.
#> ℹ Replace `OWNER/REPO` in _quarto.yml, and `OWNER` and `REPO` in the site
#>   address in _README.md, with your GitHub repository.
#> ℹ Put the paper facts in _supplement.yml.
#> ℹ Run `quarto render` in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/check-example, or
#>   `render_supplement()` in R with that folder as `path`, once before your first
#>   commit.
# A new site has not been rendered, its example report has no stored
# output yet, and it still holds the template's placeholder values.
problems <- check_supplement(site)
#> ℹ Skipped the "large-file", "saved-object", and "ignored-output" checks: `git rev-parse` failed, or the folder is not in a git work tree.
#> ✖ 11 problems found in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/check-example:
#> ✖ no-stored-output analyses/example.qmd: The report has code and no stored
#>   output in _freeze/. Render the report by name, render the whole site, then
#>   commit the report with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/. In R,
#>   render_supplement() with the report's name does both renders. If you added
#>   the report to the Analyses menu, as add_report() does, also commit
#>   _quarto.yml.
#> ✖ not-rendered docs: The site has no docs/ folder. Render the site.
#> ✖ unpublished-figure figures/bootstrap-means.png: The copy in docs/figures/ is
#>   missing or differs. Render the whole site, then commit figures/, docs/, and
#>   _freeze/.
#> ✖ placeholder _supplement.yml: Template values left in place: paper-title,
#>   citation, contact, authors. Replace them before a release.
#> ✖ placeholder _quarto.yml: The GitHub link names OWNER/REPO. Write your GitHub
#>   repository in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder index.qmd: The "Before your first commit" box is still on the
#>   home page. Delete it.
#> ✖ placeholder LICENSE.md: The copyright line reads YEAR AUTHORS. Write the year
#>   and the authors in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder LICENSE-CC-BY.md: The copyright line reads YEAR AUTHORS. Write
#>   the year and the authors in its place.
#> ✖ placeholder _README.md: The site address names OWNER and REPO. Write your
#>   GitHub account and repository in their place.
#> ✖ placeholder analyses/example.qmd: This is the template's example report.
#>   Write your own report in it, or delete it and its stored output in
#>   _freeze/analyses/example/, and make the Analyses menu in _quarto.yml list
#>   your own reports.
#> ✖ placeholder data/example.csv: This is the template's example data. Put your
#>   own data in it, or delete it, its entry under data in _supplement.yml, and
#>   the example report, which reads it.
problems$check
#>  [1] "no-stored-output"   "not-rendered"       "unpublished-figure"
#>  [4] "placeholder"        "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
#>  [7] "placeholder"        "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
#> [10] "placeholder"        "placeholder"       
unlink(site, recursive = TRUE)
